// TEST — now the mock is on the real seam
@Test fun `maps repo articles to Success`() = runTest {
  coEvery { repo.getNews("us") } returns articleList
  GetNewsListUseCase(repo).invoke("us").test {
    assertEquals(Resource.Loading, awaitItem())
    assertEquals(Resource.Success(articleList), awaitItem())
    awaitComplete()
  }
}

Pair Programming — MainViewModelTest.kt:36-37,42-49, the identical shape plus a tautological assert (§3b):

// BEFORE
newsAPI = mock()
mainViewModel = MainViewModel()                       // no arg — VM builds its own API via DependencyProvider
whenever(newsAPI.searchNews("apple")).thenReturn(mockNewsSuccess)  // stubs an object the VM never touches
mainViewModel.getNews("apple")
Assert.assertTrue(mainViewModel.news.getOrAwaitValue() is ArrayList<News>)   // tautology
// AFTER — inject the mock; assert a real outcome (see S10 in the evidence pack)
mainViewModel = MainViewModel(newsAPI)                                     // constructor injection
whenever(newsAPI.searchNews("apple")).thenReturn(Response.success(NewsResponse(articles)))
mainViewModel.getNews("apple")
assertEquals(NewsUiState.Success(articles), mainViewModel.state.getOrAwaitValue())

Review script: trace the mock. Find the mock()/mockk(), then find where the SUT is constructed. If the mock isn't passed into that constructor (or set via an injectable seam), the test is inert. Say: "the mock is never on the object's dependency path — this test exercises the real implementation."

3b. Tautological / vacuous asserts

Two flavors seen:

  • assertEquals(4, 2+2) — the auto-generated ExampleUnitTest left as the only test in 04, 02, 09, 11, 13, 14, 19, 20. It asserts the JVM can add. Zero coverage of the app.
  • assertTrue(... is ArrayList<News>) — 08 MainViewModelTest.kt:48-49. Because of type erasure this is effectively is ArrayList<*>; it can't even check the element type, and it says nothing about contents. A test that can't fail for a wrong result is worse than no test — it advertises coverage that doesn't exist. Assert the actual value: assertEquals(expectedArticles, vm.state...).

3c. Live-network / not-really-unit tests

  • 07 APIAvailabilityTest.java:14-26 opens a real HTTP connection and asserts with the Java assert keyword — which is disabled by default at JVM launch, so the "assertions" never execute and the test can never fail. Double-broken.
  • 10 ApiAvailabilityUnitTest.java opens real connections to dead endpoints (api.myjson.com).

A unit test must be deterministic and offline. Network belongs in a Retrofit-against-MockWebServer integration test (see ./05-networking-parsing.md), never in a plain unit test, and never with the disabled assert keyword — use a JUnit assertion.

3d. delay(1000) / Thread.sleep inside a test

Medibank GetNewListUsecaseTest.kt:103 does delay(1000) inside runBlocking to "wait for" the flow to collect. That's a real one-second wall-clock wait, and it's a flaky race — 1s may or may not be enough. Replace with runTest (virtual clock: delay is skipped instantly) plus deterministic collection via Turbine or advanceUntilIdle():

// BEFORE
@Test fun testUseCase() = runBlocking {
  ...
  launch { result.collect { resource.add(it) } }
  delay(1000)                                    // real 1s wait, racey
  assertEquals(Resource.Loading, resource.first())
}
// AFTER — no sleeping, no race
@Test fun testUseCase() = runTest {
  useCase.invoke("us").test {
    assertEquals(Resource.Loading, awaitItem())
    assertEquals(Resource.Success(articleList), awaitItem())
    awaitComplete()
  }
}

3e. Structural test-hygiene smells

  • Tests in src/main — 15 ships MainScreenTest.kt and : UserManagerTest.kt under app/src/main/java/.... They compile into the production APK (bloat + leaking test deps to release), and being in main they never run under ./gradlew test. Note the file literally named ": UserManagerTest.kt" (leading colon/space — an invalid, never-discovered name). Unit tests go in src/test/, instrumentation/Compose-UI tests in src/androidTest/.
  • Deprecated assert frameworks — 12 uses junit.framework.Assert and hand-rolled fakes despite Mockito being on the classpath; brittle magic asserts like size() == 3. (Credit where due: 12 is the one repo that actually tests both branches of its presenter — the positive counter-example.)
  • Removed base classes — 07 ApplicationTest extends the removed ApplicationTestCase; won't compile on modern tooling.

4. Fakes vs mocks — pick the right test double

Mock (MockK/Mockito) Fake (hand-written working impl)
What it isRecords/stubs interactions; you script return values per callA real, simplified implementation (in-memory map, canned list)
Best forVerifying interactions (was logAudit() called?), one-off stubbed returnsRepositories/APIs/DAOs with stateful behavior reused across many tests
CostCheap per test, but brittle: couples test to call signaturesSlightly more upfront code, but robust and readable
Failure modeOver-mocking → tests that assert the code called the methods you already know it calls (see 08's tautology)Fake drifts from real contract if not kept in sync

Rule of thumb: fake the things you read state from (repositories, APIs, DAOs); mock the things you verify calls to (analytics, audit logger, navigator). For a repository test double, a fake is usually clearer:

// A fake repo — no framework, trivially reusable, can model errors
class FakeReviewsRepository(
  private var result: Result<List<Review>> = Result.success(emptyList())
) : ReviewsRepository {
  fun willReturn(reviews: List<Review>) { result = Result.success(reviews) }
  fun willFail(t: Throwable) { result = Result.failure(t) }
  override suspend fun getReviews(): List<Review> = result.getOrThrow()
}
@Test fun `content on success`() = runTest {
  val repo = FakeReviewsRepository().apply { willReturn(listOf(review)) }
  ReviewsViewModel(repo).state.test {
    awaitItem()                                  // Loading
    assertEquals(ReviewsUiState.Content(listOf(review)), awaitItem())
  }
}

For faking the network boundary specifically, prefer MockWebServer over mocking Retrofit interfaces — it exercises real JSON deserialization and status handling. That's covered in ./05-networking-parsing.md.

4a. The un-mockable Kotlin object — Medibank's cousin in the testing lab

15 UserManagerTest tries to mock() the object EmailService:

object EmailService {                            // Kotlin object == final singleton
  fun sendWelcomeEmail(email: String) { println("Welcome email sent to $email") }
}
// Test attempts: mock(EmailService)  -> Mockito can't mock a final object without mock-maker-inline;
//                                        and even then you can't inject it, because it's a global.

The reason it can't be mocked is the reason it can't be injected: it's a hard-coded global singleton. The fix is the same fix as everything else in this module — introduce a seam:

interface EmailService { fun sendWelcomeEmail(email: String) }
class ConsoleEmailService : EmailService { override fun sendWelcomeEmail(email: String) = println(...) }

class UserManager(
  private val validator: UserValidator,
  private val repository: UserRepository,
  private val emailService: EmailService     // interface — now fakeable AND injectable
)
// TEST
val email = mockk<EmailService>(relaxed = true)
UserManager(validator, repository, email).register(data)
verify { email.sendWelcomeEmail("a@b.com") }   // real interaction assertion

Same shape applies to 15's Database/EmailService being objects while consumers expect instances — the graph is never assembled, and nothing is testable. See §5.

5. DI: why manual providers/singletons kill testability, and how Hilt fixes it

Every "mock never injected" and "can't mock the object" defect above is a DI defect wearing a testing costume. The through-line:

Anti-patterns seen in the repos:

  • SUT constructs its own dependency: Medibank GetNewsListUsecase.kt:24 NewsRepository(); 08 MainViewModel() builds its API via DependencyProvider; 20 new ApiImpl() / new ILoginActionImpl(this); 13 empty Application, no repo abstraction.
  • Global singletons / object: 15's Database/EmailService objects; 16's getInstance(context) manual singletons leaking Activity Context.
  • Manual ViewModelFactory threading Context through: 16 MapViewModelFactory.

Why it hurts:

  1. No seam → a test can't substitute a fake → tests either don't exist or run against real I/O.
  2. Hidden coupling → the class secretly depends on Retrofit/OkHttp/Context; you can't reason about it or reuse it.
  3. Lifecycle bugs → manual singletons that capture Context/Activity leak (16's getInstance(context), 12's presenter holding a strong Activity ref).

5a. Hilt basics (the minimum you must be able to write)

// 1. Application entry point
@HiltAndroidApp class NewsApp : Application()

// 2. Constructor injection — the class declares its real dependencies; no more `new`
class NewsRepository @Inject constructor(private val api: NewsApiService) {
  suspend fun getNews(country: String) = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { api.getTopHeadlines(country) }
}
class GetNewsListUseCase @Inject constructor(private val repo: NewsRepository) { /* uses repo */ }

// 3. Module for things you don't own / need config (Retrofit, OkHttp, Room)
@Module @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
object NetworkModule {
  @Provides @Singleton
  fun provideRetrofit(client: OkHttpClient): Retrofit = Retrofit.Builder()
    .baseUrl(BuildConfig.BASE_URL).client(client)
    .addConverterFactory(MoshiConverterFactory.create()).build()

  @Provides @Singleton
  fun provideApi(retrofit: Retrofit): NewsApiService = retrofit.create(NewsApiService::class.java)
}

// 4. ViewModel injection — no manual factory
@HiltViewModel
class NewsListViewModel @Inject constructor(
  private val getNews: GetNewsListUseCase
) : ViewModel() { /* viewModelScope.launch { ... } */ }
  • @Inject constructor — Hilt builds the object and supplies its params. This is the seam: in tests you just call the constructor with fakes/mocks yourself (no Hilt needed for unit tests).
  • @Module + @Provides — teach Hilt how to build types you can't annotate (Retrofit, OkHttpClient, interfaces). Use @Binds for interface→impl.
  • @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class) + @Singleton — scope/lifetime.
  • @HiltViewModel + hiltViewModel() (Compose) / by viewModels() (Views) — no hand-rolled ViewModelFactory (kills 16's manual-factory finding).

The payoff for testing: because every dependency arrives through a constructor, unit tests never touch Hilt — they instantiate the SUT directly with test doubles. Hilt only re-enters for instrumentation tests (@HiltAndroidTest + HiltAndroidRule + @TestInstallIn to swap modules).

5b. Medibank — "configured Hilt but fake graph" (the trap to name)

Medibank is the canonical teaching case: it has Hilt on the classpath and has modules — but the graph is fake, so it buys none of Hilt's benefits.

// BEFORE (the fake graph)
// RepositoryModule.kt:13-16 — nonsensical/circular provider; UsecaseModule injects an unused Logger
// GetNewsListUsecase.kt:24  — use case ignores DI and does `NewsRepository()` anyway
// NewsRepository.kt:16-25   — repo builds its own Retrofit/OkHttp/Moshi inline (not the provided singleton)

So Hilt is initialized, but the actual object graph is assembled by hand inside the classes with new/NewsRepository(). Result: DI present, DI benefits absent, tests still fake. The fix (evidence-pack S16) is to make the graph real — provide Retrofit→Api→Repository via @Provides/@Inject constructor, delete the bogus provideNewsRepository and the unused Logger provider, and let the use case receive the repo:

// AFTER — one real graph; the use-case test from §3a now actually exercises the mock
@Provides @Singleton fun provideRetrofit(c: OkHttpClient): Retrofit = ... .baseUrl(Constants.BASE_URL) ...
class NewsRepository @Inject constructor(private val api: NewsApiService) { ... }
class GetNewsListUseCase @Inject constructor(private val repo: NewsRepository) { /* repo, not `new` */ }

Interview line: "Hilt being on the classpath is not the same as using it. Here the classes still new their dependencies, so the DI is decorative — I'd expect the mock in the use-case test to be dead, and it is." That connects the DI finding to the testing finding in one breath — exactly the cross-cutting insight reviewers reward.

6. Self-check

Answer these before the round; each maps to a real repo finding.

  1. A MainViewModelTest creates newsAPI = mock() then mainViewModel = MainViewModel(). What's wrong, and how do you know it before reading the ViewModel? (Mock is never injected — the no-arg ctor means the VM builds its own API; the stub is dead. → 08, §3a.)
  2. assertTrue(vm.result is ArrayList<News>) — why is this near-worthless? (Type erasure makes it is ArrayList<*>; asserts nothing about contents; can't fail for a wrong result. → §3b.)
  3. A test rule imports TestCoroutineScope and calls cleanupTestCoroutines(). What do you say? (Removed in coroutines-test 1.7; replace with TestWatcher + TestDispatcher + runTest. → 03, §2a.)
  4. Why does Dispatchers.setMain(...) matter when testing a ViewModel? (viewModelScope uses Dispatchers.Main, which throws on the JVM unless a test Main dispatcher is installed. → §2.)
  5. delay(1000) in a test under runBlocking — what breaks and what's the fix? (Real 1s wall-clock + flaky race; use runTest virtual clock + Turbine. → §3d.)
  6. Test files under app/src/main/java/... — name two consequences. (Shipped in the APK; never executed by ./gradlew test. → 15, §3e.)
  7. mock(EmailService) where EmailService is a Kotlin object — why does it fail, and what's the root fix? (Final singleton, unmockable and un-injectable; extract an interface + inject it. → §4a.)
  8. "The repo uses Hilt, so DI is fine." Rebut using Medibank. (Hilt configured but classes still new their deps → graph is fake, tests inert. → §5b.)
  9. When do you fake vs mock a dependency? (Fake state you read from — repos/APIs/DAOs; mock things you verify calls to — analytics/audit/nav. → §4.)
  10. Where does a Retrofit-against-real-JSON test belong, and why not in a unit test? (Integration layer via MockWebServer; unit tests must be offline/deterministic. → §3c, ./05-networking-parsing.md.)

Drill: take 04's MyNewsActivity or 09's RestaurantsActivity, extract the logic into a Repository + ViewModel with constructor-injected dependencies, then write the three ViewModel tests (Loading→Content, Loading→Error, and a mapper edge case). If you can't write the test, the DI isn't done. More timed drills in ./07-mock-drills.md; API/imports quick-reference in ./08-cheatsheets.md.

17.7 Mock Drills & Interviewer Q&A

The code-review round is a performance, not just an analysis. Interviewers score three things independently:

  1. Coverage — did you find the real blockers (crash, ANR, leak, security)?
  2. Prioritization — did you fix/flag the right things first, under time?
  3. Communication — could they follow your reasoning out loud?

You can find every bug and still fail on (2) and (3). These drills train all three. Run them against the real cloned repos as if the clock were ticking.

How to use this module

  • Pick a drill. Set a hard timer — put your phone face-down at the far end of the desk.
  • Open the target repo in Android Studio (or just read the files listed). Do not open its SOLUTION.md until your timer ends.
  • Narrate out loud the whole time (see Talking out loud). Record yourself if you can.
  • When the timer rings, stop typing. Open the <details> Reveal block and self-score.
  • The reveal cites the canonical findings; the full write-up is the repo's SOLUTION.md (linked in each drill).

Global rubric shape (each drill customizes point values, total 100):

  • Blockers found (crash/ANR/leak/security) — the bulk of the points.
  • Prioritization — did P0 come before P2?
  • Communication — clear, specific, file:line, proposed fix.
  • Bonus — tests, positives called out, "what I'd do with more time".

Drill 1 — OneFootball: review-as-PR (45 min)

Target: ../04-onefootball-coding_challenge_android/ · single file app/src/main/java/com/onefootball/MyNewsActivity.kt.

Scenario framing. "A candidate submitted this take-home. Review it as a PR. Would you merge it? List your blocking comments, then your non-blocking suggestions." This is the classic review-as-PR format — you are the senior on the team.

Time box: 45 min. Suggested split: 10 min read the whole file top-to-bottom, 20 min write findings, 10 min prioritize + verdict, 5 min pick the one fix you'd pair on.

Tasks:

  1. Produce a prioritized findings list (P0 blockers → P3 nits), each with file:line + a one-line fix.
  2. Give a merge verdict with a one-sentence justification.
  3. Call out at least 2 things the candidate did right (interviewers watch for this — pure negativity reads as junior).
  4. Name the single highest-leverage refactor and sketch its target shape.
Reveal — expected findings

P0 blockers (all in MyNewsActivity.kt):

  • Main-thread file I/O + JSON parse in onResume() → ANR — :36-47. Runs on every resume.
  • No try/catch around asset read / parse → guaranteed crash on any I/O or schema drift — :38-45.
  • inputStream.read(buffer) return value ignored → truncated-read/parse crash — :41. Fix: assets.open("news.json").bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }.
  • Unguarded startActivity(ACTION_VIEW) → ActivityNotFoundException — :86-90. Guard with resolveActivity.
  • God Activity + zero real tests — the actual deliverable. No ViewModel/repo/DI; only assertEquals(4, 2+2).

Highest-leverage refactor: extract NewsRepository (asset read on Dispatchers.IO) + a pure NewsParser + a NewsViewModel exposing StateFlow<UiState>. Activity only observes. Load-once survives rotation and becomes unit-testable.

Positives to name: proper data class News, RecyclerView + ViewHolder, Coil for images, INTERNET permission declared, adapter exposes a clean setNewsItems(...).

Verdict: Not ready — ANR + guaranteed crash paths are merge blockers regardless of the missing architecture.

Scoring (100): ANR find 20 · crash-no-try/catch 15 · truncated-read 10 · unguarded intent 10 · god-Activity/no-tests 15 · correct P0-first ordering 10 · ≥2 genuine positives 10 · clear proposed fixes with file:line 10.

Drill 2 — Agilevent: debug the launch crash / ANR (30 min)

Target: ../05-agilevent-android-job-application-challenge-2/ · MainActivity.java (Java, Eclipse/Ant era). The README states three seeded bugs: (1) crashes on launch, (2) UI doesn't match screenshot, (3) ANRs on slow networks.

Scenario framing. "This app crashes the instant you open it. Here's a device. Find why, tell me the root cause, and tell me the fix — you don't have to type the whole solution." This is the debug-under-time format: interviewers want a hypothesis-driven approach, not a shotgun read.

Time box: 30 min. Split: 5 min reproduce/read the crash path, 10 min root-cause all three README bugs, 10 min propose fixes, 5 min "what else is wrong" sweep.

Tasks:

  1. State the root cause of the launch crash in one sentence.
  2. Explain why bug (1) and bug (3) share a single root cause.
  3. Find the NPE that fires when the request fails.
  4. Explain the UI mismatch (bug 2).
  5. Propose the minimal safe fix, then say what you'd do "properly."
Reveal — expected findings
  • Launch crash = network on the main thread + StrictMode death. MainActivity.java:34-43 installs StrictMode with detectAll() + penaltyDeath(); :52-56 does a synchronous DefaultHttpClient().execute(get) in onCreate on the UI thread → NetworkOnMainThreadException, and penaltyDeath() kills the process.
  • Bugs 1 and 3 are the same defect. The blocking main-thread call crashes on modern SDKs (bug 1) and, absent StrictMode, would ANR on slow networks (bug 3). Fixing it off-thread fixes both. Note AsyncTask is imported (:14) but never used — the fix was scaffolded, never wired.
  • NPE on failure — response is null (:54); catch blocks only printStackTrace() and fall through to :66 response.getStatusLine() → NPE. Fix: check status / null-guard before deref.
  • UI mismatch — adapter sets only the top line top.setText(commit.author.name) (:106); the bottom TextView (:104) is fetched but never populated, so the commit message never shows.
  • Bonus: dead GitHub v2 cleartext endpoint :53 (never returns 200 even once threaded); leaked InputStream/Scanner/connection (:67,:77); removed org.apache.http stack (deleted in API 23).

Minimal fix: move the fetch into an AsyncTask.doInBackground (or better, a background thread), drop penaltyDeath(), null-guard response, bind both TextViews. Proper: Retrofit/OkHttp + ViewModel + repository + Gson converter + loading/error state.

Scoring (100): identify main-thread-network root cause 25 · connect bugs 1↔3 to one cause 15 · NPE-on-failure find 15 · UI mismatch (unbound TextView) 15 · propose off-thread fix that also drops penaltyDeath 15 · spot dead endpoint OR resource leaks 10 · (Java-specific awareness: says "AsyncTask/Handler here, coroutines if this were Kotlin") +bonus.

Drill 3 — GetYourGuide: pair refactor (45 min, live)

Target: ../03-getyourguide-android-challenge/ · ReviewsFragment.kt. Compose reviews list; "works in the happy path only."

Scenario framing. Pair-programming. An interviewer sits with you. "This works but isn't built with best practices. Let's improve it together — talk me through what you'd change and let's do the first refactor live." You are expected to think aloud, take direction, and actually write code (or pseudocode) for at least one change.

Time box: 45 min. Split: 10 min read + narrate the smells, 5 min agree with interviewer on the first move, 25 min do the extraction live, 5 min "if we had another hour."

Tasks:

  1. Verbally inventory the top smells before touching the keyboard.
  2. Propose an ordered refactor plan and get buy-in on step 1.
  3. Live-refactor the GlobalScope.launch in setContent into a ViewModel with viewModelScope and a UiState (Loading/Content/Error).
  4. Handle the date-parse crash and add an error branch as you go.
Reveal — expected findings
  • GlobalScope.launch inside setContent → leaks + re-fires the network call on every recomposition — ReviewsFragment.kt:62-65. Not lifecycle-scoped, not cancellable.
  • No error handling on api.getReviews() — :63. Any failure/timeout/parse error crashes or leaves an infinite spinner; no error UiState exists.
  • Crash-prone date parse LocalDateTime.parse(review.created, ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssz")) — :105-108. Throws on Z/offset/fractional seconds and is recomputed every recomposition. Fix: tolerant OffsetDateTime.parse in a mapping layer, runCatching, done once.
  • No architecture / no DI — networking + state + UI in onCreateView; Retrofit built inline (RetrofitBuilder.kt:15, ReviewsApi.kt:7).
  • Eager Column + verticalScroll for up to 60 items (should be LazyColumn); Spacer used as a divider.
  • Tests won't compile — TestCoroutineRule.kt uses removed TestCoroutineScope/Dispatcher.

Target for the live step (from the evidence pack, snippet S1):

class ReviewsViewModel(private val repository: ReviewsRepository) : ViewModel() {
  private val _state = MutableStateFlow<ReviewsUiState>(ReviewsUiState.Loading)
  val state: StateFlow<ReviewsUiState> = _state.asStateFlow()
  init { load() }
  fun load() = viewModelScope.launch {
    _state.value = ReviewsUiState.Loading
    _state.value = runCatching { repository.getReviews() }
      .fold({ ReviewsUiState.Content(it) }, { ReviewsUiState.Error(it.message ?: "…") })
  }
}

Scoring (100): name the GlobalScope recomposition bug 20 · propose ViewModel+viewModelScope+UiState 20 · actually write compiling-ish extraction 20 · add Error state 10 · fix/notice the date parse 10 · collaboration signals (ask before choosing step 1, accept a redirect, verbalize tradeoffs) 20. In a pair round, communication is worth as much as the code.

Drill 4 — Halan: fix the crash, then refactor + test (60 min)

Target: ../06-halan-fixing-refactoring_challenge-task/ · starter commit 7361b46 (detached HEAD — do not use master, which is the finished solution). Java. Login → products list → detail. AsyncTask + AndroidNetworking, god activities.

Scenario framing. Fix-then-refactor with tests. "The app crashes right after a successful login. Fix the crash first, then improve the login flow and add a test that would have caught this." Two-phase: stop the bleeding, then leave it better than you found it.

Time box: 60 min. Split: 15 min reproduce + root-cause the post-login NPE, 15 min minimal fix, 20 min extract a testable seam + write one test, 10 min list remaining debt.

Tasks:

  1. Root-cause the guaranteed NPE after login.
  2. Explain the LoginTask threading bug and why navigation "sometimes" doesn't happen.
  3. Apply the minimal correct fix (put the missing extra; return the real result; navigate on the main thread).
  4. Extract enough of a seam that you can unit-test the login-result mapping without Android.
  5. Name the second network stack and why having two is a smell.
Reveal — expected findings
  • Guaranteed NPE after login — LoginTask never puts the RESPONSE extra, so ProductsListActivity reads a null bundle and dereferences loginResponse.profile.image — ProductsListActivity.java:41-55.
  • Threading + navigation bug — LoginTask.onPostExecute(true) is called inside doInBackground (:66) → startActivity on a background thread; and doInBackground unconditionally return false (:74), so the framework's real onPostExecute never navigates. (Snippet S5.)
  • No error handling — switch(status) handles only 200, no default/error branch — :63-67.
  • Two network stacks — raw HttpURLConnection + AsyncTask for auth and AndroidNetworking for products; hardcoded URLs, no timeouts/retry.
  • God activities — parse + net + adapter wiring in onCreate; ProductDetailsActivity derefs a possibly-null bundle and sets no LayoutManager on the images RV (images never render); notifyDataSetChanged() before setAdapter (:80-81).

Minimal fix (S5):

if (success) {
  Intent i = new Intent(context, ProductsListActivity.class);
  i.putExtra("RESPONSE", result);   // the missing extra the consumer reads
  context.startActivity(i);          // main thread; no FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK for in-app nav
}

Test seam: pull the "parse login JSON → LoginResponse" and the "decide navigation target" logic out of the AsyncTask into a plain class/function; unit-test it with a fake JSON string (no device needed). That test would have caught the missing-profile NPE.

Scoring (100): root-cause the missing-extra NPE 25 · explain the onPostExecute-in-doInBackground bug 20 · minimal fix puts extra + navigates on main thread 15 · extract a testable seam 15 · write one meaningful test 15 · spot the double network stack / no-error-branch 10.

Drill 5 — Medibank: full PR review with a written verdict (60 min)

Target: ../01-medibank-ventures-code-review-exercise-android/ · Kotlin, Compose, Moshi/Retrofit/Hilt. This one is a modern stack — the bugs are subtler and more senior.

Scenario framing. Full written PR review. "Here's a take-home. Write the PR review you'd actually post: blocking comments, non-blocking suggestions, and a merge decision. The team uses Hilt and coroutines." The trap: it looks production-grade, so you must not be fooled by the presence of DI/Flow.

Time box: 60 min. Split: 15 min read the graph (DI wiring, ViewModel, repo), 25 min write findings, 10 min security/hygiene sweep, 10 min verdict + summary comment.

Tasks:

  1. Trace the DI graph and decide whether it's real or theatre.
  2. Find the coroutine-scope lifecycle bug.
  3. Find the test that passes for the wrong reason.
  4. Do a secrets/hygiene pass.
  5. Write the top-of-PR summary comment (2-3 sentences) you'd post.
Reveal — expected findings
  • Hardcoded API key committed — common/Constants.kt:6 (API_NEWS_TOKEN). In git history and the APK. P0 security. Fix: BuildConfig from local.properties/CI, rotate the key.
  • DI is theatre — GetNewsListUsecase.kt:24 does NewsRepository(); the repo builds Retrofit inline (NewsRepository.kt:16-25); RepositoryModule.kt:13-16 provider is nonsensical/circular; Logger provider unused. Hilt is configured but the graph is fake and untestable. (Snippet S16.)
  • ViewModel scope leak — hand-rolled CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + Job()) never cancelled in onCleared() — NewsListViewModel.kt:23-24,38. Should be viewModelScope. (Snippet S2.)
  • Test passes by accident — GetNewListUsecaseTest.kt:36 mocks the repo, but the use case constructs its own, so the mock is never exercised; uses delay(1000) instead of a TestDispatcher. (The canonical "mock never injected" case.)
  • Requirement gap — brief wants user-selected sources; app hardcodes country="us" with a dead setCountry() — NewsListViewModel.kt:29.
  • Model nullability — non-null domain title/url from nullable DTO via .orEmpty() → blank URL → blank WebView (Article.kt:11,12 vs ArticleDto.kt:20-24). Dead XML/nav resources from the pre-Compose app.

Verdict: Not ready — leaked secret + fake DI + scope leak are individually blocking.

Scoring (100): find the committed API key 20 · diagnose fake-DI (not just "uses Hilt, looks fine") 25 · scope-leak find 15 · test-passes-for-wrong-reason find 15 · requirement gap 10 · a crisp, non-hostile summary comment 15. Docking: minus 15 if you praised the DI as good because Hilt is present — the whole point is that its presence is misleading.

Drill 6 — MCR / JLR: Compose + XML refactor with a correctness bug (45 min)

Target: ../02-mcrmobile-Android-Refactoring/ · Kotlin, two modules: compose/ (preferred) and xml/. JLR vehicles list. Two backlog tickets: JLR-1234 (filter to Land Rover), JLR-1235 (detail screen).

Scenario framing. Refactor across paradigms. "We have the same feature in a Compose module and an old XML module. Review both, find the correctness bug, and tell us how you'd add architecture. Then implement ticket JLR-1234." Tests your ability to work in both Compose and classic Views and to read requirements, not just code.

Time box: 45 min. Split: 10 min diff the two modules, 15 min findings + the correctness bug, 10 min JLR-1234 plan, 10 min architecture sketch.

Tasks:

  1. Find the user-visible correctness bug in the XML module's binding.
  2. Find the adapter crash risk.
  3. Explain why rotation re-fetches the network in the Compose module.
  4. State what's needed to satisfy JLR-1234 (brand filter) and JLR-1235 (detail).
  5. Sketch the ViewModel/UiState you'd add to both modules.
Reveal — expected findings
  • Wrong bound text — xml/.../VehiclesFragment.kt:69 binds model + " " + model (should be brand + " " + model). User-visible.
  • Adapter crash risk — vehicles[adapterPosition] (can be NO_POSITION = -1) + requireContext() in the click listener — VehiclesFragment.kt:52-62.
  • Rotation re-fetch — LaunchedEffect(Unit) in a non-rememberSaveable composable re-fires the network on every rotation; no ViewModel/UiState.
  • JLR-1234 unmet — neither module filters by brand, so Jaguar shows among Land Rover.
  • JLR-1235 unmet — tap only shows a Toast (compose MainActivity.kt:62-68); the XML Vehicle model even lacks the vin field (VehiclesService.kt:18-26).
  • No architecture — logic in Composable/Fragment; silent catch { printStackTrace() }; no loading/error/empty UI; Coil declared but unused; items(vehicles.size) index-based with no stable key.

Architecture sketch: a shared VehiclesViewModel exposing StateFlow<VehiclesUiState>, fetch in viewModelScope, filter brand == "Land Rover" in the repo/use-case (JLR-1234), pass vin through the model and navigate to a detail destination (JLR-1235). Compose observes with collectAsStateWithLifecycle; XML observes via repeatOnLifecycle.

Scoring (100): find model + model bug 20 · adapter NO_POSITION crash 15 · rotation-refetch cause 15 · JLR-1234 filter plan 15 · JLR-1235 (missing vin) 10 · ViewModel/UiState sketch for both modules 15 · stable-keys/LazyColumn detail 10.

Talking out loud (pair-programming rounds)

In a pair round the interviewer is scoring your process, not your silence. Bad candidates read in silence for 8 minutes then say "this is bad." Strong candidates externalize a loop. Use this script:

1. Orient (30–60s). Say what you're looking at and how you'll attack it.

"Single-Activity app, all logic in MyNewsActivity. I'll skim top to bottom for lifecycle and threading first, then correctness, then style. Let me start in onResume."

2. Narrate the scan as a running commentary. Every time you form a hypothesis, say it before you confirm it.

"This is assets.open … in onResume … on the main thread. That's a red flag — file I/O on the UI thread is an ANR risk, and it re-runs on every resume. Let me confirm nothing hops threads … no, no dispatcher. So P0: main-thread I/O."

3. Prioritize out loud. Explicitly rank as you go so the interviewer hears your judgment.

"I'm calling that a blocker. The hardcoded strings I noticed are a nit — I'll park them and come back if we have time."

4. Ask before you commit to a direction. In a pair, alignment beats speed.

"I see three things I'd refactor: the scope, the error handling, and the date parse. I'd start by hoisting the network call into a ViewModel because it fixes the leak and gives us a place for error state. Does that ordering work for you, or would you rather see the crash fixed first?"

5. Think in tradeoffs, not absolutes. Seniority shows in "it depends."

"I'd reach for StateFlow over LiveData here since we're Compose-first, but LiveData would be fine and needs less test setup. I'll go StateFlow."

6. When stuck, say what you're doing. Silence reads as being lost.

"I want to check how the extra is passed — give me ten seconds to find where the Intent is built."

7. Land the plane. Before time's up, summarize.

"So: two blockers — the GlobalScope leak and no error handling; one correctness bug in the date parse; the rest is architecture debt. With more time I'd add a repository interface and a ViewModel state test."

Anti-patterns that cost points: narrating every keystroke ("now I type val"); silent reading; only listing negatives with no positives; rewriting everything instead of the one thing asked; arguing with a redirect instead of taking it and moving.

Interviewer Q&A

Practice saying each answer aloud in under 60 seconds. Ground every claim in a concrete case — that's what separates a senior answer from a textbook recital.

Q1. "How would you make this testable?"

Answer. Introduce seams: an interface for the data source, constructor injection for dependencies, and a pure function for parsing/mapping. Right now logic is welded to the Android framework — e.g. OneFootball parses inside MyNewsActivity using assets/org.json, so there's nothing to unit-test without a device. I'd extract NewsRepository (interface) + a pure NewsParser + a ViewModel that takes the repository in its constructor. Then I test the parser with plain JUnit, the ViewModel with a fake repository and a TestDispatcher. Talking points: interface at the boundary; constructor over field injection; pure functions for logic; fakes over mocks for your own interfaces. See 06-testing-di.md.

Q2. "Where's the ANR risk here?"

Answer. Anywhere blocking work runs on the main thread. Three canonical shapes in these repos: file I/O — OneFootball reads and parses news.json in onResume (MyNewsActivity.kt:36-47); network — Agilevent does a synchronous DefaultHttpClient call in onCreate (MainActivity.java:52-56); artificial blocking — the ImageSearch repo does Thread.sleep(2000) in a click handler (13/MainActivity.kt:38-47); and DB/disk — Kakao opens writableDatabase and reads synchronously on the main thread (16/KeywordDao.kt:8-50). Fix: move to Dispatchers.IO via a coroutine in a ViewModel, or Room suspend/Flow for the DB. Talking points: the 5-second window; StrictMode as a detector; withContext(Dispatchers.IO).

Q3. "GlobalScope vs viewModelScope — why does it matter?"

Answer. GlobalScope is unbounded and not tied to any lifecycle, so its coroutines leak and can outlive the screen, and — as in GetYourGuide, ReviewsFragment.kt:62 — if you launch it inside setContent it re-fires on every recomposition. viewModelScope is cancelled automatically in onCleared(), so the work dies with the ViewModel. Pair Programming (08/MainViewModel.kt:16) even imports viewModelScope and then uses GlobalScope anyway. The fix is always: launch in viewModelScope (or lifecycleScope for UI-only work), never GlobalScope. Talking points: structured concurrency; cancellation propagation; @DelicateCoroutinesApi is a warning, not a suggestion. See 04-concurrency-lifecycle.md.

Q4. "How do you handle API nulls / a field that might be missing?"

Answer. Model the wire shape as nullable, then map to a clean domain model at a boundary. Pair Programming's News.kt:6-15 declares author/urlToImage/content non-null and publishedAt: Date, so Gson NPEs or throws on the real newsapi.org response that returns nulls and ISO-8601 strings. Make DTO fields nullable (author: String?), keep dates as String (or use an adapter), and map to a domain type where you decide defaults explicitly — not with a silent .orEmpty() that turns a null URL into a blank WebView, like Medibank's Article.kt. For manual parsing (News App MediaEntity.java), use optString/optInt with defaults instead of getString/getInt that throw. Talking points: DTO ↔ domain separation; nullable at the edge, non-null in the core; tolerant parsing. See 05-networking-parsing.md.

Q5. "MVVM vs MVP — which and why?"

Answer. For new Android I default to MVVM with a ViewModel + unidirectional state (StateFlow<UiState>), because the ViewModel survives config changes and integrates natively with Compose and lifecycle-aware collection — no manual view detach. MVP still works (the Books repo, 12, uses a presenter with view/repository interfaces and a real presenter test), but its classic weakness shows there too: the presenter holds a strong Activity reference with no detach/dispose (BooksActivityPresenter.java:10-16) → leak. MVVM sidesteps that. I'd use MVP only in a legacy codebase already built on it. Talking points: state survival across rotation; view-detach discipline in MVP; UDF; both are testable if you keep the view behind an interface.

Q6. "How do you decide what to fix first?"

Answer. By blast radius. P0 = things that crash, ANR, leak, or leak secrets — user- or security-impacting and non-negotiable. P1 = correctness bugs (wrong data shown, requirement unmet). P2 = architecture/testability. P3 = style/hygiene. Concretely, in Medibank I'd fix the committed API key and the fake DI before I touch Color.Blue hardcoding. In OneFootball the ANR and the guaranteed crash come before "split the adapter into its own file." I state the ranking out loud so the interviewer hears the judgment, and I park nits explicitly rather than silently skipping them. Talking points: crash/ANR/leak/security first; requirement gaps count as bugs; time-box the nits. See 01-code-review-method.md.

Q7. "This uses Hilt — so DI is fine, right?"

Answer. Not necessarily — presence isn't correctness. Medibank has Hilt fully configured but the graph is theatre: the use case does NewsRepository() directly (GetNewsListUsecase.kt:24), the repo builds Retrofit inline (NewsRepository.kt:16-25), and the module provider is circular/nonsensical (RepositoryModule.kt:13-16). Nothing is actually injected, so nothing is swappable in a test — which is exactly why its use-case test passes without ever exercising the mock. I always trace the graph: is the dependency received via constructor, or constructed inside? Kakao is the analogue — Hilt and Room on the classpath, entirely unused in favor of manual factories. Talking points: constructed-vs-injected; DI's payoff is test seams; classpath presence ≠ usage.

Q8. "What's wrong with catching an exception and calling printStackTrace()?"

Answer. It hides failures from both the user and your telemetry. GetYourGuide, MCR, Kakao, and News App all swallow network errors with printStackTrace() (or an empty Rx error consumer in 09/RestaurantsActivity.kt:126), so a failed fetch shows an infinite spinner or an empty list with no way to recover. Errors should become an explicit UiState.Error the UI renders (with retry) and should be logged to your crash/analytics pipeline. Silent catch is only acceptable when you genuinely have a fallback value and you comment why. Talking points: error UiState + retry; log to Crashlytics/Timber; never catch (e: Exception) {}.

Q9. "How would you fix the crash on a null Intent extra / result?"

Answer. Never treat framework-provided extras as non-null. Pair Programming does intent.getSerializableExtra("newsSelected") as News (DetailActivity.kt:22) — crashes on null or wrong type. The Kotlin refactor repo declares onActivityResult(..., data: Intent) non-null, but Android passes null on cancel (14/MainActivity.kt:34). Fix: use a nullable type (data: Intent?), a null-safe getter (getParcelableExtraCompat<News>(KEY) ?: return), a constant key shared between writer and reader (the 14 repo writes PERSON and reads the literal "PERSON"), and prefer @Parcelize/Parcelable over Serializable. Talking points: nullable at the boundary; shared key constants; Parcelable over Serializable; type-safe nav args.

Q10. "AsyncTask everywhere — how would you modernize it?"

Answer. AsyncTask is deprecated and leak-prone — it captures the enclosing Activity/Fragment and its callbacks fire after detach (PetApp, 10, NPEs on nulled mContext/mListener; Halan calls onPostExecute inside doInBackground, running startActivity on a background thread). In Kotlin I'd replace it with coroutines: suspend functions in a repository on Dispatchers.IO, launched from viewModelScope, results as StateFlow. In a Java codebase that can't adopt coroutines yet, at minimum make it a static inner class holding a WeakReference and check for detach, or use ExecutorService + Handler — but the real answer is coroutines/Flow. Talking points: lifecycle capture; detach-time callbacks; coroutines + repository as the target.

Q11. "Where do you put the API key / how do you handle secrets?"

Answer. Never in source. Medibank commits the key in Constants.kt:6 — it's now in git history and the APK. The correct pattern is exactly what Pair Programming does right: read it from local.properties/CI into BuildConfig, then inject it via an OkHttp ApiKeyInterceptor. Kakao does the same via getApiKey(...) → BuildConfig/resValue. And once a key has been committed, rotating it is part of the fix — scrubbing the file isn't enough because it's in history. Talking points: local.properties → BuildConfig; interceptor injection; rotate leaked keys; .gitignore hygiene.

Q12. "This test passes — is it a good test?"

Answer. Passing isn't the bar; exercising the right code is. Two failure modes in these repos: the mock is never injected — Medibank (GetNewListUsecaseTest.kt:36) and Pair Programming (MainViewModelTest.kt:36-50) both create a mock but the subject constructs its own real dependency, so the test hits the network and passes by accident; and tautological assertions — Pair Programming asserts the result is ArrayList<News>, which is always true. A good test injects a fake, drives one behavior, and asserts a specific expected value (a UiState.Success(expected)), and it controls time with a TestDispatcher instead of delay(1000). Talking points: inject the double; assert specifics not types; runTest + TestDispatcher; test the error branch too (Turbine for Flow). See 06-testing-di.md.

Q13. "How would you prevent the list from re-fetching on rotation?"

Answer. Hoist the fetch above the Activity's lifecycle. MCR re-fetches because LaunchedEffect(Unit) runs on each recomposition/recreation and there's no state holder; OneFootball reloads in onResume; News App refetches on rotation because the raw Thread lives in the Activity. Move the load into a ViewModel that fetches once in init (or a guarded load()), expose StateFlow, and collect it with collectAsStateWithLifecycle. The ViewModel survives rotation, so the data is cached across config changes for free. Talking points: ViewModel survives config change; LaunchedEffect(Unit) ≠ once-ever; SavedStateHandle for process death.

Q14. "notifyDataSetChanged() everywhere — does it matter?"

Answer. Yes — it rebinds every visible row, drops animations and scroll position, and is O(n) even for a one-item change. It shows up in 02/04/06/08/09. The fix is ListAdapter + DiffUtil: submitList(newList) diffs off the main thread and rebinds only what changed. Watch the companion trap: adapterPosition/bindingAdapterPosition can be NO_POSITION (-1) after a change, and indexing list[position] or getItem(-1) then crashes (MCR VehiclesFragment.kt:52, ImageSearch PhotoAdapter.kt:45) — guard for RecyclerView.NO_POSITION in click listeners. Talking points: DiffUtil/ListAdapter; stable keys; NO_POSITION guard.

Q15. "Would you merge this PR? Justify in one sentence."

Answer. State a verdict, then the single most important reason. "No — a synchronous main-thread network call in onCreate crashes the app on launch, so nothing else matters until that's off-thread" (Agilevent). Or "No — the API key is committed to source and history, which is a security incident regardless of code quality" (Medibank). The interviewer wants a decisive call plus evidence, not "well, it depends." If it's genuinely close, say what the one change is that would flip you to yes. Talking points: decisive verdict; lead with the top blocker; name the flip condition.

Q16. "You have 20 minutes and this whole app is a mess. What do you do?"

Answer. Triage, don't boil the ocean. First 5 min: read for the P0s — anything that crashes, ANRs, or leaks a secret. Next 10: fix or precisely document those, and pick the one structural change with the highest leverage (usually hoisting logic out of the Activity into a ViewModel, because it unblocks threading, error state, and testing at once). Last 5: write the punch list of everything I didn't get to, ranked, so the reviewer knows I saw it. Explicitly say "I'm parking the styling and the toolchain bump" so skipping them reads as a choice, not a miss. Talking points: P0 sweep first; one high-leverage refactor; a ranked "not done" list; verbalize your parking decisions.

Q17. "The app reads from a WebView — any concerns?"

Answer. Yes — unvalidated URLs are an injection/redirect surface. PetApp (10) loads an arbitrary JSON-provided content_url into a WebView and its shouldOverrideUrlLoading re-loads any URL with no allowlist. I'd validate the scheme/host against an allowlist, disable JavaScript unless required, avoid addJavascriptInterface with untrusted content, and never load http://. Medibank's news links similarly flow into a WebView — those should at least be https and origin-checked. Talking points: URL allowlist; disable JS by default; no addJavascriptInterface for remote content; https only.

Q18. "What did the candidate do right?" (or: "Is anything here good?")

Answer. Always have this ready — it signals you review fairly. OneFootball uses a proper data class, RecyclerView + ViewHolder, and Coil for images. Pair Programming injects its API key correctly via a BuildConfig interceptor. Kakao reads keys from local.properties and debounces search input. Better-Android (09) actually gets Rx threading right and disposes its CompositeDisposable in onDestroy. Calling these out shows I'm evaluating the code, not just pattern-matching for bugs — and it makes the blocking feedback land better. Talking points: fairness; specific positives by file; feedback lands better when balanced.

Self-check

Before you walk into the round, confirm you can do each of these from memory in one minute:

  • [ ] Give a verdict + top blocker for any one repo above, in one sentence.
  • [ ] Name the four P0 categories (crash, ANR, leak, security) and one real example of each.
  • [ ] Explain GlobalScope vs viewModelScope with the GetYourGuide recomposition example.
  • [ ] Explain why Hilt being present ≠ DI being real using the Medibank graph.
  • [ ] Explain why a passing test can be worthless (mock never injected / tautology).
  • [ ] Rattle off the modernization target: ViewModel + StateFlow<UiState> + repository interface + coroutines on Dispatchers.IO + DiffUtil + inject secrets via interceptor.
  • [ ] Run Drill 2 (Agilevent) end-to-end in under 30 minutes and score ≥ 70.
  • [ ] Narrate a 90-second think-aloud on OneFootball's onResume without reading from notes.

If you can do all eight, you're ready. If not, re-run the drill for the weakest one and consult the linked module.

1. The 10-Minute Review Checklist (printable)

Run top-to-bottom. Each line is a pass; each pass answers one question. Budget ~1 min/pass.

[ ] 0. SCOPE (30s)  Does the subject code exist & compile? What's the branch/entry point?
                     -> 18 was an empty scaffold; 15/20/11 do NOT compile. Establish this first.
[ ] 1. BUILD/DEPS   jcenter()? kotlin-android-extensions? dead SDK/AGP? unused deps (Glide+Coil)?
[ ] 2. SECRETS      Hardcoded API keys? cleartext http? committed .idea/? passwords/PII in source?
[ ] 3. ENTRY CLASS  Open the main Activity/Fragment/Composable. Is it a "god" class (net+parse+UI)?
[ ] 4. THREADING    Any I/O/network/parse on main thread? GlobalScope? hand-rolled scope? AsyncTask?
[ ] 5. LIFECYCLE    viewModelScope/lifecycleScope? cancel on onCleared? observeForever removed?
                     Rotation: does it re-fetch / lose state? LaunchedEffect(Unit)?
[ ] 6. ERROR PATHS  try/catch on I/O? loading/error/empty UI states? status-code checks? swallow?
[ ] 7. MODELS       Non-null fields from a nullable API? Date type vs ISO-8601 string? Parcelable?
[ ] 8. CRASH SCAN   !!, unchecked casts, getExtras()!!, adapterPosition/NO_POSITION, index-by-position
[ ] 9. ARCH/DI      ViewModel? repository? Hilt real or faked? mock actually injected in tests?
[ ] 10. TESTS/UI    Real assertions or 2+2? tests in src/main? RecyclerView 0dp? DiffUtil vs notifyAll?

Time-box variant (if you only have 5 min): run passes 0, 3, 4, 6, 8 — scope, god class, threading, error paths, crash scan. Those five catch the blockers in almost every repo (e.g. 04 ANR + no try/catch, 08 GlobalScope + crash-on-null, 06 background-thread startActivity).

3. Smell → Fix Quick Table

One line each. → = the standard fix. Links point at the catalog section.

Smell Fix
GlobalScope.launch→ viewModelScope.launch (see concurrency)
Hand-rolled CoroutineScope in VM→ viewModelScope; delete onCleared scope juggling
I/O on main thread→ withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { … } in a repository
AsyncTask→ coroutines + repository, or WorkManager for deferred work
No try/catch on network→ runCatching { … }.fold(…) → UiState.Error
printStackTrace()→ log + emit an error state the UI renders
Non-null model from nullable API→ make fields nullable; map with defaults at the boundary
publishedAt: Date from JSON→ keep as String?, format in a mapper with runCatching
Unchecked as News cast→ getParcelableExtra<News>(KEY) ?: return (typed, null-safe)
getExtras()!! NPE→ null-check the bundle; ?: finish()
!! in comparator→ sortedBy { it.distance }
adapterPosition in click→ bindingAdapterPosition, guard == NO_POSITION
Parallel arrays by index→ a single model / data class list
notifyDataSetChanged()→ ListAdapter + DiffUtil (stable keys)
Retrofit built inline→ single @Provides @Singleton via Hilt/DI
Hardcoded API key→ BuildConfig from local.properties/CI + rotate
Stringly-typed type + when no-else→ sealed class / enum with @DrawableRes
Hand-rolled Parcelable→ @Parcelize data class
Mock created but not injected→ constructor-inject the dependency
LaunchedEffect(Unit) re-fetch→ fetch in viewModelScope in init; expose StateFlow
observeForever→ LiveData/Flow scoped to lifecycle; remove observer
God Activity/Fragment→ extract ViewModel → repository → data source
jcenter()→ mavenCentral() / google()
Cleartext http://→ https://; never disable cleartext policy

4. Code Snippets (copy-paste ready)

4a. Coroutine scope quick-ref

Scope Lives in Cancelled when Use for
viewModelScopeViewModelonCleared()screen data loads (default)
lifecycleScopeActivity/FragmentdestroyUI-only work tied to the view
viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScopeFragment viewview destroyedFragment view work (avoid the fragment scope for view work)
repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)collectorstops in backgroundcollecting a Flow in the UI safely
GlobalScopeprocessnever❌ almost never — a red flag
CoroutineScope(...) customyouyou must❌ in a VM; leaks (01)
// UI-safe Flow collection (replaces observeForever / GlobalScope in composables)
lifecycleScope.launch {
    repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
        viewModel.state.collect { render(it) }
    }
}

4b. UiState sealed class + ViewModel (the canonical fix — from 03, 08)

sealed interface UiState<out T> {
    data object Loading : UiState<Nothing>
    data class Content<T>(val data: T) : UiState<T>
    data class Error(val message: String) : UiState<Nothing>
}

class ReviewsViewModel(private val repo: ReviewsRepository) : ViewModel() {
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow<UiState<List<Review>>>(UiState.Loading)
    val state: StateFlow<UiState<List<Review>>> = _state.asStateFlow()

    init { load() }

    fun load() = viewModelScope.launch {
        _state.value = UiState.Loading
        _state.value = runCatching { repo.getReviews() }
            .fold({ UiState.Content(it) }, { UiState.Error(it.message ?: "Something went wrong") })
    }
}

Compose side renders the three states — no data == null spinner heuristic, no crash on failure.

4c. Retrofit + Result (safe call, tolerant model)

// Nullable DTO at the boundary (real API returns nulls: 08/News.kt, 01/Article.kt)
@JsonClass(generateAdapter = true)
data class ArticleDto(
    val title: String?,
    val url: String?,
    val publishedAt: String?,   // keep as String; parse in the mapper, never Date in the DTO
)

// Repository does IO + maps to a clean domain model
class NewsRepository @Inject constructor(private val api: NewsApi) {
    suspend fun getNews(country: String): Result<List<Article>> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        runCatching {
            api.getTopHeadlines(country).articles.orEmpty().map { it.toDomain() }
        }
    }
}

fun String?.toDisplayDate(): String =            // fixes 03's crash-prone LocalDateTime.parse
    runCatching { OffsetDateTime.parse(this) }
        .map { it.format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MMM dd, yyyy")) }
        .getOrDefault("")

4d. Hilt annotations quick-ref

@HiltAndroidApp        class MyApp : Application()          // 1. mark the Application
@AndroidEntryPoint     class MainActivity : ...             // 2. mark the injection target
@HiltViewModel         class NewsViewModel @Inject constructor(private val repo: NewsRepository) : ViewModel()
class NewsRepository   @Inject constructor(private val api: NewsApi)   // constructor injection = default

@Module @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
object NetworkModule {
    @Provides @Singleton
    fun provideRetrofit(client: OkHttpClient): Retrofit =   // provide types you don't own
        Retrofit.Builder().baseUrl(BASE_URL).client(client)
            .addConverterFactory(MoshiConverterFactory.create()).build()

    @Provides fun provideApi(retrofit: Retrofit): NewsApi = retrofit.create(NewsApi::class.java)
}

// @Binds (in an abstract @Module) to bind an interface to its impl:
@Binds abstract fun bindRepo(impl: NewsRepositoryImpl): NewsRepository
Symptom in the repo Diagnosis
GetNewsListUsecase does NewsRepository() (01:24)DI present but faked — Hilt configured, graph bypassed
RepositoryModule.provideNewsRepository circular (01:13)nonsensical provider — delete it, use @Binds/constructor
Hilt on classpath, manual ViewModelFactory (16)DI unused entirely

4e. Testing setup snippet (coroutines + Turbine + Mockito-Kotlin)

@OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)
class MainDispatcherRule(
    private val dispatcher: TestDispatcher = StandardTestDispatcher()
) : TestWatcher() {
    override fun starting(d: Description) = Dispatchers.setMain(dispatcher)
    override fun finished(d: Description) = Dispatchers.resetMain()
}

class ReviewsViewModelTest {
    @get:Rule val mainRule = MainDispatcherRule()

    @Test fun `emits Error when repository fails`() = runTest {
        val repo = mock<ReviewsRepository> { onBlocking { getReviews() } doThrow IOException("boom") }
        ReviewsViewModel(repo).state.test {                  // Turbine
            assertThat(awaitItem()).isInstanceOf(UiState.Error::class.java)
        }
    }

    @Test fun `injected mock is actually used`() = runTest {
        val api = mock<NewsApi>()                            // fixes 08/01: INJECT the mock
        whenever(api.getTopHeadlines("us")).thenReturn(NewsResponse(articles))
        val vm = MainViewModel(api)                          // <-- constructor injection, not new inside
        vm.getNews("us")
        verify(api).getTopHeadlines("us")
    }
}

Note: modern kotlinx-coroutines-test (1.7+) uses runTest/TestDispatcher — the removed TestCoroutineScope/TestCoroutineDispatcher in 03/TestCoroutineRule.kt won't compile. Deeper patterns in ./06-testing-di.md.

5. Architecture Decision Quick-Ref (which pattern when)

Situation Pick Rationale
New screen, Kotlin, coroutines/FlowMVVM + repositoryidiomatic default; viewModelScope, StateFlow, testable
Reactive streams, filter/sort/combineMVVM + Flow (or Rx)operators upstream, not on main (09)
Legacy Java, RxJava already presentMVP (interface + presenter)minimal seam retrofit; but tie dispose to lifecycle (12)
Multiple screens sharing domain logicClean-ish: + UseCase layerreuse + testable business rules
One-off tiny app, single screenMVVM without a UseCase layerdon't over-engineer — repository is enough
Local persistenceRoom (suspend/Flow DAO)off-thread by default; kills raw-SQLite main-thread I/O (16)
Deferred/guaranteed background workWorkManagersurvives process death; not AsyncTask/Thread
DIHiltstandard; constructor injection first, modules for types you don't own
UI extra passing@Parcelize + typed key constantnot Serializable, not literal keys (08, 14)
List UIListAdapter + DiffUtil (or LazyColumn)not notifyDataSetChanged() (02/04/06/08/09)

Rule of thumb to say out loud: "Add layers to create a testing seam and move work off the main thread — not for their own sake." Full treatment in ./03-architecture-mvvm-clean.md.

6. Interview Talking-Points / Soft-Skills One-Pager

How to prioritize (say this framing)

"I'll triage into blockers (crashes, ANRs, security, data loss), major (architecture/testability/error handling), and minor (naming, style, dead code). I'll fix or flag blockers first."

Concrete blocker examples to name: main-thread I/O ANR (04), guaranteed crash-on-null (08, 06), leaked secret (01), doesn't compile (11/15/20).

How to state a verdict

Use one of three, and commit:

  • ❌ Not ready / request changes — has blockers. "I'd request changes: the hardcoded key and the main-thread parse are merge blockers."
  • ⚠️ Approve with comments — no blockers, but majors. "Approve once the GlobalScope→viewModelScope and error-state changes land."
  • ✅ Approve — clean (rare in these exercises).

Always: verdict → top 3 reasons → what would change your mind.

How to disagree / handle pushback

  • Anchor on impact, not taste: "This isn't style — getExtras() returns null on a cancelled result, so this NPEs 100% of the time." (07/14)
  • Concede cheaply: "Fair, the enum is a nice-to-have; the null-safety is the must-fix."
  • Offer the trade: "If we're tight on time, keep the manual parse but at least wrap it in try/catch and add the IO dispatcher."
  • Ask before assuming: for 18 (empty scaffold) the right move was "there's no subject code — can you confirm the repo/branch?" — not inventing findings.

Narration habits that score points

  • Read the entry class first, out loud: "Everything's in MyNewsActivity — that's my architecture finding."
  • Cite file:line. "MainViewModel.kt:16, GlobalScope."
  • Separate correctness ("this crashes") from quality ("this is hard to test").
  • State the fix, not just the flaw. Every finding = problem → impact → fix.
  • Time-box aloud: "I'll spend 2 more minutes on tests then summarize."

Method depth: ./01-code-review-method.md.

7. Glossary

Term Meaning (Android context)
ANRApplication Not Responding — main thread blocked >5s; caused by I/O/network/Thread.sleep on UI thread (04, 05, 13).
viewModelScopeCoroutine scope auto-cancelled in ViewModel.onCleared(). Correct replacement for GlobalScope/hand-rolled scopes.
lifecycleScopeScope tied to a LifecycleOwner (Activity/Fragment); cancelled on destroy.
repeatOnLifecycleRestarts a block when lifecycle enters a state (e.g. STARTED); the safe way to collect Flows in UI.
GlobalScopeProcess-lifetime scope; never cancelled → leaks. Red flag.
StateFlow / SharedFlowHot Kotlin Flows for exposing UI state / events from a ViewModel.
UiStateSealed type modeling Loading/Content/Error(/Empty) so the UI is exhaustive and can't forget an error path.
DiffUtil / ListAdapterComputes minimal RecyclerView updates; replaces notifyDataSetChanged().
adapterPosition / NO_POSITIONViewHolder position; returns -1 (NO_POSITION) transiently → indexing crash. Use bindingAdapterPosition + guard.
@ParcelizeKotlin plugin that generates Parcelable; use for intent extras instead of Serializable/hand-rolled Parcelable.
HiltJetpack DI (Dagger-based). @HiltAndroidApp, @AndroidEntryPoint, @HiltViewModel, @Module/@Provides/@Binds.
RepositoryLayer that owns data access (network/db), does IO off-thread, returns domain models. Provides the test seam.
UseCase / InteractorSingle business action; sits between ViewModel and repository in Clean architecture.
DTO vs domain modelDTO mirrors the wire format (nullable, ISO strings); domain model is clean/non-null. Map at the boundary.
DI "present but fake"Hilt/modules exist but code still news dependencies, so the graph is bypassed and untestable (01).
TurbineTest library for asserting emissions from a Flow.
runTest / TestDispatcherModern kotlinx-coroutines-test API (1.7+); replaces removed TestCoroutineScope/Dispatcher.
MainDispatcherRuleJUnit rule swapping Dispatchers.Main for a TestDispatcher so viewModelScope works in unit tests.
jcenterDeprecated/shut-down artifact registry; builds referencing it fail to resolve.
kotlin-android-extensionsDeprecated plugin (synthetics/@Parcelize); migrate to ViewBinding + kotlin-parcelize.
Cleartext trafficUnencrypted http://; blocked by default on modern targetSdk.
God classOne class doing networking + parsing + state + UI; the dominant architecture smell across these repos.
observeForeverObserves LiveData without a lifecycle; leaks unless removeObserver is called (16).

Cover the right column; answer from memory. If you miss more than 3, re-read the linked module.

Which 5 passes catch most blockers under time pressure?Scope, god class, threading, error paths, crash scan (passes 0/3/4/6/8).
Repo has no reviewable code (18) — what do you do?Don't invent findings; confirm the repo/branch/scope with the interviewer.
catch { printStackTrace() } — why flag it?Silent failure: no user feedback, no error state, hides real bugs. Emit a UiState.Error.

Drill it: ./07-mock-drills.md runs timed scenarios against these exact cues.

Books

The following books are cited or recommended throughout the study guide.

"The Threading Book" (cited throughout topics.md)

The study guide repeatedly references a concurrency/Android threading book covering:

  • Part I — Process and thread fundamentals in Android
  • Producer-consumer patterns
  • Handler / Looper / MessageQueue internals
  • Thread-induced memory leaks (static inner classes, weak references)
  • Stopping and retaining worker threads
  • Cleaning up message queues

The exact title is not recorded in the source. The description most closely matches one of:

  • "Android Concurrency" — G. Blake Meike (covers HandlerThread, Looper, AsyncTask)
  • "Efficient Android Threading" — Anders Göransson (O'Reilly, ISBN 978-1449364137) — covers all cited topics and is the most widely referenced Android-specific threading book; most likely match

Search ISBN 9781449364137 or title "Efficient Android Threading" to locate it.

Kotlin

  • Effective Kotlin — Marcin Moskala (Kt. Academy)
    • Best practices for null safety, coroutines, collections, performance
    • https://kt.academy/book/effectivekotlin
  • Kotlin in Action — Dmitry Jemerov & Svetlana Isakova (Manning)
    • Comprehensive Kotlin language guide

Java / JVM

  • Effective Java (3rd edition) — Joshua Bloch (Addison-Wesley)
    • Items on equals/hashCode, generics, enums, concurrency — directly tested in interviews
    • https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/effective-java/9780134686097/
  • Java Concurrency in Practice — Brian Goetz et al. (Addison-Wesley)
    • The definitive reference for JMM, visibility, atomicity, Executor framework, wait/notify
    • Core for Section 3 and Section 4 questions

Architecture / System Design

  • Clean Architecture — Robert C. Martin
    • Dependency rule, layer boundaries, use cases — directly maps to Section 7
  • Designing Data-Intensive Applications — Martin Kleppmann (O'Reilly)
    • Distributed systems trade-offs; useful for senior system-design questions in Section 15
  • Staff Engineer — Will Larson
    • Technical leadership, influence without authority — useful context for Section 18 answer framing
    • https://staffeng.com/book
